Docs.summary: Provides the legacy interface projection of the Apache HTTP status constants.
Docs.remarks: The constants also appear on . This interface has no instance members. Its constants include historical HTTP and WebDAV codes, not a complete registry of current status codes.
The request was accepted for processing, but processing has not finished. This status does not guarantee eventual success.
A gateway or proxy received an invalid response from the upstream server.
The server could not understand the request because its syntax was invalid.
The request conflicts with the resource's current state. The client can resolve the conflict before sending the request again.
This interim response permits the client to send the rest of the request. A final response follows after the request is complete.
The request completed and created a new resource. The response can identify its location.
The server cannot meet the request's Expect header requirement, or a proxy has clear evidence that the next server cannot meet it.

Docs.summary: The WebDAV 424 Failed Dependency status code.
Docs.remarks: The operation could not run because another action on which it depended failed.
The server understood the request but refused to perform it.
A gateway or proxy did not receive a response in time from a server needed to complete the request.
The resource is no longer available, no forwarding address is known, and the condition is expected to be permanent.

Docs.summary: The 505 HTTP Version Not Supported status code.
Docs.remarks: The server cannot or will not use the HTTP major version in the request.

Docs.summary: The historical WebDAV draft 419 Insufficient Space on Resource code.
Docs.remarks: This value comes from section 10.4 of draft-ietf-webdav-protocol-05. It describes insufficient space to record the resource's state after an operation; it is not the 507 code defined by RFC 2518.

Docs.summary: The WebDAV 507 Insufficient Storage status code.
Docs.remarks: The server cannot store the representation needed to complete the request. RFC 2518 describes this condition as temporary.

Docs.summary: The 500 Internal Server Error status code.
Docs.remarks: An unexpected server condition prevented the request from being completed.
The server requires a defined Content-Length before it accepts the request.
A source or destination resource needed by the operation is locked.

Docs.summary: The historical WebDAV draft 420 Method Failure code.
Docs.remarks: Section 10.5 of draft-ietf-webdav-protocol-05 uses this value when a failure in one part of a method causes the whole method to stop. It is not the 424 code defined by RFC 2518.

Docs.summary: The 405 Method Not Allowed status code.
Docs.remarks: The request method is not permitted for this resource. The response's Allow header lists the permitted methods.
The resource has a new permanent URI. Future references should use the new URI.

Docs.summary: The 302 Found status code, named Moved Temporarily by this API.
Docs.remarks: The resource is temporarily at another URI. Future requests should still use the original URI.
The resource has multiple representations from which the user or client can select.
The response body gives separate status results for multiple operations or resources.
The request completed without a response body. Response headers can still contain updated resource metadata.
The response metadata came from a local or third-party copy rather than directly from the origin server.
The resource cannot produce a response that meets the content preferences in the request's accept headers.
No resource matching the request URI was found. This status does not establish whether the absence is permanent.
The server does not support functionality needed to perform the request.
A conditional retrieval found no change to the resource. The response has no message body.
The request succeeded. The request method determines what information the response contains.
The server fulfilled a range request and returns the selected part or parts of the resource.
RFC 2616 reserves this code for future use and defines no payment protocol for it.
At least one condition supplied in the request headers evaluated to false at the server.
This interim response indicates that the full request was accepted but is still being processed. A final response is still required.

Docs.summary: The 407 Proxy Authentication Required status code.
Docs.remarks: The client must authenticate with the proxy. The Proxy-Authenticate header supplies the challenge.

Docs.summary: The 416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable status code.
Docs.remarks: The requested ranges do not overlap the selected resource's current extent.
The client did not send its request within the time the server allowed.

Docs.summary: The 413 Request Entity Too Large status code.
Docs.remarks: The request body exceeds what the server is willing or able to process.

Docs.summary: The 414 Request-URI Too Long status code.
Docs.remarks: The server refuses to process a request URI whose length exceeds what it will interpret.
The request completed and the client should reset the view used to submit it. The response has no entity body.
The result can be retrieved with a GET request to a different URI identified by the response.
The server is temporarily unable to handle the request because of overload or maintenance.
The server agrees to switch to the protocol identified in the response's Upgrade header.
The resource is temporarily at another URI. Redirecting the request must not silently change its method.
The request needs authentication. The WWW-Authenticate response header supplies a challenge for the resource.

Docs.summary: The WebDAV 422 Unprocessable Entity status code.
Docs.remarks: The server understands the request body's format and syntax but cannot process its instructions.

Docs.summary: The 415 Unsupported Media Type status code.
Docs.remarks: The request body uses a format that the target resource does not support for the requested method.
RFC 2616 uses this code to direct the request through the proxy identified by the Location header.
